messages:
maya r.: Heads up, I found a bunch of odd failures in the fallback flow when routing by tier+region. Looks like tokenizer + tool-calling parity is causing invisible regressions for some customers.
jon h.: Ugh. Which variants/regions?
maya r.: EU region hitting variant `redwood-v2-small-q8` as fallback for Standard tier — a few requests ended up with truncated tool args. Root cause looks like different tokenization (byte vs bpe) + context off-by-n.
liam_w: Can you paste an example?
maya r.: Sure — original prompt (hosted model):
```
{"user_input":"Call getInvoice for order #987654321 with payment.method = \"card\", attachReceipt: true"}
```
When routed to the fallback variant the function call blob becomes split across tokens and we send a truncated JSON blob to the tool.
priya s.: That's the classic tokenizer parity issue. Are we normalizing to the same tokenizer at router time?
maya r.: No, router currently only checks architecture/size compatibility and max_seq length. We only verify tool schemas at model registry time if the model advertises function-calling support. No per-variant tokenizer parity check.
jon h.: Two problems: (1) tokenization changes effective token counts -> quota/billing differences; (2) tool-calling schema may be functionally present but tokenization can break JSON encoding.
infra-bot: NOTE: recent deploy 2026-02-17 03:02 UTC added `fallback-routing-v2` policy to canary clusters.
liam_w: For immediate mitigation: can we route by a new metadata flag `tokenizer_family` + `tool_call_compat=true/false`? If a fallback lacks parity we skip it for tiers with strict contracts (Gold/Enterprise).
priya s.: +1. Also add `max_context_bytes` to model metadata — byte-length check avoids off-by-token surprises when different encoders map to different bytes.
jon h.: We should also reflect this in the Console rollout UX. When creating a rollout rule you could see a compatibility score and a hard-block toggle for tiered customers. UX mock: "Show compatibility: Tokenizer: mismatch (BPE vs byte-level), Tool-calls: partial, Context: 4k vs 3.2k" with a red warning.
maya r.: I sketched a telemetry query we can add to ops dashboards to surface incidents:
```
SELECT count(*) as failures, model_variant, region
FROM tool_call_logs
WHERE tool_response_status = 'invalid_payload'
  AND payload_parse_error LIKE '%unexpected end%'
  AND timestamp >= now() - interval '30 days'
GROUP BY model_variant, region
ORDER BY failures desc
LIMIT 50;
```
liam_w: Nice. We should also compute token_delta = router_estimated_tokens - model_actual_tokens per request and aggregate by variant to catch systemic deltas.
priya s.: Implementation checklist I propose:
- Add `tokenizer_family` + `max_context_bytes` + `tool_call_schema_hash` to model catalog metadata (string fields)
- Router: match by tokenizer_family for same-tier routing; if mismatch, tiered policy decides allow/deny
- Console: compatibility score + hard-block toggle in rollout wizard
- Telemetry: add token_delta metric and invalid_tool_payload dashboard panel
- Migration: backfill catalog for existing variants and run parity checks (dry run)
jon h.: For quotas: if token_delta > 0 often when falling back, we need to surface a warning to billing team — falling back could double-charge tokens on some requests if tokenizer splits differently.
maya r.: Agreed. Also one gotcha: quantized variants can change tokenization surface because of trimming hooks in our runtime; add runtime flags to metadata: `runtime_trim_behavior` (none|aggressive).
infra-bot: ACTION: Created ticket INF-3142 to add model metadata fields and router checks.
priya s.: I'll take the Console changes. Liam can you own router check + telemetry? Jon, can you coordinate with billing on token_delta alert? Maya will validate failing samples and produce a short repro harness.
liam_w: Yup, I'll start with a lightweight check that filters out incompatible variants from Gold tier rollouts, then extend to other tiers.
jon h.: I'll ping finance for prioritization. If this impacts enterprise SLAs we may want an emergency opt-out toggle.
maya r.: Thanks team. I'll drop a sampling of failing payloads in the ticket. Small ask: log original token boundaries (router vs model) for 2% of traffic to avoid over-logging.
priya s.: Done, I'll update the rollout mock in Figma and add the "compatibility breakdown" panel.
maya r.: Closing the loop here — follow-ups in INF-3142 and PRs after the dry-run. :thumbsup:
